mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) when both triggers are met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate hiring, which in turn leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO MoM < -1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained industrial production decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent fall in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two months signals a deep monetary easing and deflationary risk, which historically has been associated with positive equity risk premia and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months
regime_hint: deep monetary easing and deflation risk
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.10) when both triggers are met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) above its 5-year moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in consumption-driven growth and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5-year moving average +10% for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of elevated real savings.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payrolls (PAYEMS) month-over-month, where UNRATE increases by >0.3pp and PAYEMS decreases by >1% MoM, signals a situation of rising unemployment despite falling employment, which typically occurs during mass layoffs and foreshadows negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both triggers are met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 8% for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average +8% for five months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of sustained housing starts acceleration.
